title: Interlocks and permissives: a guard that stops the motor
summary: Add a permissive to a motor start and stop so that the motor runs only while a guard is closed, and check it against the motor plant and its speed feedback.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence for a built-in motor plant model with one 10 ms task; they do not establish a safety function, guard wiring, stopping time, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Tell a permissive, a condition that must be true for the output to be on, from a command.
Put a permissive in the same condition that holds the motor, so that it drops the motor and also stops Start from restarting it.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/MotorPlant.st the first assignment holds Command with a seal-in and the second sets Running when the plant reports AtSpeed. Add GuardClosed with AND to the first assignment, so that an open guard drops Command and blocks Start.
stages.checkpoint: Command is on only while the guard is closed, and Running still needs the plant's AtSpeed.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict Command and Running at {{t:30}} ms, when the guard opens at {{t:50}} ms, and at {{t:60}} ms when Start is pressed with the guard still open.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:MotorPlant.Command=true,MotorPlant.Running=true@30|Both ON}} at {{t:30}} ms; {{v:MotorPlant.Command=false,MotorPlant.Running=false@50|both OFF}} at {{t:50}} ms; {{v:MotorPlant.Command=false@60|Command OFF}} at {{t:60}} ms, because Start is ignored.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press Check: The starter has no permissive on the guard, so when the guard opens at {{t:50}} ms the motor keeps running and Start can restart it; add AND GuardClosed to the whole condition of Command, outside the brackets that hold Start and Command.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the motor plant answering your outputs.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named MotorInterlock and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:30}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:80}} ms: the motor is at speed at {{t:30}} ms, drops when the guard opens at {{t:50}} ms, and does not restart at {{t:80}} ms when the guard closes, because Start was released.
stages.checkpoint: Command stays OFF from {{t:60}} to {{t:80}} ms and rises again only at {{t:90}} ms, with a new Start.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Why is a permissive on the whole condition safer than a permissive only on Start? Put GuardClosed next to Start and see which assertion fails.
stages.checkpoint: A permissive that gates only Start lets a running motor ignore an open guard. The scenario shows the logic only; it is not a safety function and does not replace a certified guard interlock.

hints.text: Command may be TRUE only if the guard is closed, Stop is not pressed, and either Start is pressed or Command was already TRUE.
Command := (Start OR Command) AND NOT Stop AND GuardClosed; Do not put GuardClosed inside the brackets with Start.

faultCases: The starter has no permissive on the guard, so when the guard opens at {{t:50}} ms the motor keeps running and Start can restart it; add AND GuardClosed to the whole condition of Command, outside the brackets that hold Start and Command.
